speaker: Unknown
en: And so we learned some hard lessons about making something people actually want.
zh: 所以我们就打造一些人们真正想要的东西这一方面，吸取了惨痛的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think I've been able to apply at Paper.
zh: 然后我想我已经能够将其应用到 Paper 中。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we did make, I mean, the Radix has amazing product market fit.
zh: 但我们确实做到了，我是说，Radix 拥有惊人的产品市场契合度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just didn't see a way to build like a venture scale business around it.
zh: 我们只是没看到围绕它建立一家风投规模业务的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we thought, let's just make it free and give it away and then, you know, come back with something next time.
zh: 所以我们想，不如把它免费做出去分发掉，然后，你知道，下次带着新东西回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's been cool.
zh: 所以那很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that worked out really well.
zh: 我是说，结果真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We sold this company to WorkOS, which is an amazing auth and identity company.
zh: 我们把这家公司卖给了 WorkOS，这是一家很棒的身份认证和身份管理公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use WorkOS for paper.
zh: 我们在 Paper 上使用 WorkOS。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a couple of years after that, I just wanted to start back into creative tooling again.
zh: 然后在那几年后，我只是想重新开始做创意工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And are there any lessons that you took from that experience that you're applying this time?
zh: 你从那段经历中学到了什么教训，正在这次应用吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can way overcomplicate product building.
zh: 你可能会把产品构建搞得过于复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the make something people want is a great phrase.
zh: 你知道，「做出人们想要的东西」是一句很棒的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really, a lot of times with your product, it's like, what does my company need next?
zh: 实际上，很多时候对于你的产品来说，就像是这样，我的公司接下来需要什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would be like the best thing that possibly could happen to my company right now?
zh: 现在对我的公司来说，可能发生的最好的事情是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: At the beginning for us, that was like being part of the conversation, having Twitter followers.
zh: 对我们来说，起初那就像参与对话、拥有 Twitter 粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, let's go do things that get Twitter followers.
zh: 那我们就去做那些能获得 Twitter 粉丝的事情吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go on a podcast.
zh: 去上播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's talk to users and then represent their values outwardly.
zh: 和用户交谈，然后对外代表他们的价值观。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of times it's actually very simple.
zh: 所以很多时候其实非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we make it too complicated.
zh: 而我认为我们把它搞得太复杂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're trying to have these brilliant strategies for our companies.
zh: 我们试图为我们的公司制定这些高明的策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, what do you need next?
zh: 就像这样，你接下来需要什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And just do the most straightforward thing you can possibly do to get there.
zh: 然后就做你能做到的最直接的事情来达到目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't be scared to do things that sound hard.
zh: 不要害怕去做那些听起来很难的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, you've got to do them.
zh: 显然，你必须做这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the philosophy we've taken.
zh: 所以这就是我们要采取的哲学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bottlenecks first.
zh: 瓶颈优先。

speaker: Unknown
en: Huge, huge philosophy I really believe in.
zh: 这是一个巨大的、巨大的哲学，我真的非常相信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like for us right now, the bottleneck is early adopters are using paper.
zh: 就像对我们现在来说，瓶颈是早期采用者正在使用 Paper。

speaker: Unknown
en: The people that are more, you know, maybe not an early adopter type are very used to what they're doing now.
zh: 那些更，你知道，也许不是早期采用者类型的人非常习惯他们现在正在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're missing features like comments and components.
zh: 而且他们缺少像评论和组件这样的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now our bottleneck is actually features again.
zh: 所以现在我们的瓶颈实际上是功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now it's like, well, that's what we got to go do next.
zh: 所以现在就像这样，那就是我们接下来必须去做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And release that bottleneck to the business.
zh: 并释放那个业务瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another just like a tactical thing is just like talking to users every day.
zh: 另一个战术性的事情就是每天都要和用户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so, so important.
zh: 这非常、非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a rule.
zh: 我有一个规矩。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first year of the company, I had to talk to a designer every single day.
zh: 公司的第一年，我每天都要和一位设计师交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I did it all the way through the year.
zh: 而且我坚持了一整年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was so useful because I learned just how
zh: 那非常有用，因为我了解到

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when you start making the company and the product, you just have a different perspective.
zh: 就像当你开始创建公司和产品时，你只是有一种不同的视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't help that.
zh: 你无法避免。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a curse of knowledge.
zh: 你有知识的诅咒。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so just staying rooted in user conversations is really important.
zh: 所以保持扎根于用户对话中真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It gets harder and harder to do that as the company grows and scales also because there's so many other things that are vying for your time and pulling you in different directions and that seem important or hair on fire in the moment.
zh: 随着公司的发展和壮大，这样做会变得越来越难，因为有太多其他的事情在争夺你的时间，把你往不同的方向拉扯，而且看起来很重要或是火烧眉毛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But really it's those core fundamental things of build your product, talk to users.
zh: 但实际上就是那些核心的基础的东西，构建你的产品，与用户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, exercise or whatever you need to do so you don't go crazy doing the first few things.
zh: 然后，你知道，锻炼或者做任何你需要做的事，这样你在做前几件事时才不会发疯。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's the core of it for the life of the company, right?
zh: 但这就是公司生命周期内的核心，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's cool to hear that you've done that from the very first day.
zh: 所以很高兴听到你从第一天起就这样做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm sure it is something that has been instilled culturally in your team now and that everybody is talking to users at this point.
zh: 我确信这现在已经融入你们团队的文化中了，每个人现在都在与用户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah, yeah.
zh: 哦，是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When people onboard, it's like, yeah, you have to be in the Discord talking to people or in the Slack.
zh: 当人们入职时，就像这样，是的，你必须在 Discord 里与人交谈，或者在 Slack 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really, really important.
zh: 这真的、非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not everyone's comfortable.
zh: 并不是每个人都舒服。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they've come from a bigger company where they were told they can't talk to users.
zh: 也许他们来自一家大公司，在那里他们被告知不能与用户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, no, get in there.
zh: 这就像是，不，进去吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't screw it up.
zh: 你搞不砸的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you just learn so much.
zh: 而且你能学到很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it guides your decision making.
zh: 我认为这能指导你的决策制定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Decisions are really important in a company.
zh: 决策在公司中真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can kind of look at successful companies of like, you can trace their decisions backwards in time of like, oh, that was an inflection point.
zh: 你可以看看成功的公司，比如，你可以追溯它们随时间推移的决策，比如，噢，那是一个拐点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That decision was really good.
zh: 那个决策真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having an informed employee base, like I can't make every decision in the company.
zh: 拥有一名见多识广的员工基础，就像我无法做出公司里的每一个决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even at 12 people, there's no way I could do that.
zh: 即使在 12 人的时候，我也没办法那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you can have your employees be really informed about users and what they actually want, you'll have good decisions being made all over, you know, all over the place.
zh: 所以如果你能让你的员工对用户以及他们真正想要的东西非常了解，那么到处都会做出好的决策，你知道，到处都是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, it's really important.
zh: 是的，这真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: MARK MANDELMAN- What do you think is next for design?
zh: MARK MANDELMAN- 你认为设计接下来是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think a lot of design isn't changing.
zh: 嗯，我认为很多设计并没有改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, in orgs, it's like the function of design is still really important as a way to explore problem space, competitive analysis, executive stakeholders, things like this.
zh: 同样，在组织中，就像是设计的功能仍然非常重要，作为一种探索问题空间、竞争分析、执行利益相关者、诸如此类的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not seeing that change at all.
zh: 我们完全没有看到那一点改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that function of design, I think, is sticking around.
zh: 所以设计的那个功能，我认为，会保留下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: If anything, I think we're going to see more because there are more companies and there's more software to be made.
zh: 如果有什么的话，我认为我们会看到更多，因为有更多的公司，有更多的软件要制作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're seeing just more and more design need in the world.
zh: 所以我们看到世界上越来越多的设计需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think the tooling is going to accelerate because I think we just need to be able to keep the quality bar up at a pace that is keeping up with the engineering, with the product teams.
zh: 我确实认为工具将会加速，因为我认为我们只需要能够保持质量标准在一个跟得上工程和产品团队的步伐上。

speaker: Unknown
en: The software will ship whether the designer gets a chance to make it better or not.
zh: 软件都会发布，无论设计师是否有机会让它变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is kind of like a reality of the competitive landscape.
zh: 这有点像是竞争格局的现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do we help make sure that the designer can be part of the conversation and keep up in that shipping process?
zh: 那么我们要如何帮助确保设计师能够成为对话的一部分并在那个发布过程中跟上？

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think in general,
zh: 但我认为总的来说，

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes I think there's less change coming than people think, actually.
zh: 有时我认为即将到来的变化比人们想象的要少，实际上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think that a lot of design is a very human problem, and the pixels at the end are like the output of the process.
zh: 因为我认为很多设计是一个非常人性化的问题，而最后的像素就像是过程的输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the medium at the end of the day, right?
zh: 它毕竟是媒介，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly, yeah.
zh: 确实，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's next for paper?
zh: Paper 接下来是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, so we are, like I said, we're building out some table stakes, components, comments, bottleneck reducers.
zh: 嗯，就像我说的，我们正在构建一些基本要素、组件、评论、瓶颈消除器。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited.
zh: 我真的很兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something I've learned from talking to users is people are building all these prototypes all over the place.
zh: 我从与用户交谈中学到的一件事是，人们到处都在构建这些原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're ending up on Vercel or their HTML files.
zh: 它们最终会出现在 Vercel 上或者他们的 HTML 文件中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people don't know how to leave feedback onto them, how to even find which one someone's talking about.
zh: 人们不知道如何在这些原型上留下反馈，甚至不知道如何找到某人在谈论的那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we're going to do is we're going to put, basically, you can like iframe things onto the paper canvas as a place to keep your prototypes kind of like organized.
zh: 所以我们要做的是，基本上，你可以把像 iframe 的东西放到 paper 画布上，作为一个让你的原型保持有条理的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then people can leave comments as they're used to doing on the prototypes.
zh: 然后人们可以像他们习惯在原型上做的那样留下评论。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when people ask us if we're doing prototyping, it's like, well, kind of.
zh: 所以当人们问我们是否在做原型设计时，就像是，嗯，有一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to help you organize your prototypes and have feedback cycles.
zh: 我们要帮助你整理你的原型并拥有反馈循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this is going to be a really big unlock for companies that are building playgrounds for their designers to vibe code in.
zh: 我认为对于那些正在为设计师建立游乐场以进行 vibe coding 的公司来说，这将是一个非常大的解锁。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then it's kind of like this messy result.
zh: 但随后这就像是一个杂乱的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they need some tool to help them organize that.
zh: 他们需要一些工具来帮助他们整理这些内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's a big thing we're going to be working on the next six months or so as we're building out the table stakes that people expect to.
zh: 所以这是我们将在接下来的六个月左右着重做的一件大事，正在构建人们期望的那些基本要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: MARK MANDELMANN- Amazing.
zh: MARK MANDELMANN- 太棒了。

en: Stephen, thank you so much for coming on and sharing paper with us and all of your design insight that I know has been hard earned over the years and the companies that you've built and the incredible places you've worked.
zh: Stephen，非常感谢你来到这里与我们分享 paper，以及分享你的所有设计见解，我知道这些是你在过去几年里，在你构建的公司和你工作过的令人难以置信的地方中辛苦得来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you.
zh: 所以谢谢你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, thank you so much for having me.
zh: 是的，非常感谢你们的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: That does it for this episode of Design Review, and we'll see you on the next one.
zh: 本期 Design Review 就到这里，我们下期见。
